clue.text: US city centre in which tons of food circulates

indicators.note: the centre word takes the following pieces inside it, so these words mark a container

parts.note: the pith is the central core of something
T is the abbreviation for ton, so tons is TS

indicators.note: something that circulates goes round, so the food word is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Food is passed around at a feast in the middle of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulates' turns GRUB into BURG; 'in which' puts TS and BURG inside PITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pittsburgh is a large city in Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Short course in Italian history

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter of the dish goes

parts.note: pasta is a course in an Italian meal

explanation.surface: A brief study module on Italian history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of PASTA. 'Course' looks academic but it is a part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The past means what has gone before: history.

clue.text: The drinks are on one? No good, just kidding

indicators.note: being on something means sitting before it here, so the drinks word is placed ahead of the one letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone claims a round is on them, then admits it was a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are on' places the drinks before the one; the surface reads it as someone paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing someone is playfully kidding them.

clue.text: Sergeant Major's special skill — appearing thus?

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for Sergeant Major
an art is a special skill

explanation.surface: A sergeant major's talent is looking neat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: a sergeant major is expected to look smart.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant major is famous for a neat, well-turned-out look.

clue.text: Stock initially depleted? One's ruined

indicators.note: the stock word loses its first letter, its initial

parts.note: a fund is a stock of money

explanation.surface: With supplies running low at the start, a person faces ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially depleted' takes F off FUND; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undone has been brought to ruin.

clue.text: Environmental group finally abandoned drink

indicators.note: the final letter of the group word is dropped

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigning group ended up giving up its efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally abandoned' drops M from TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is a drink made from unoxidised tea leaves.

clue.text: Hairstyle adopted by Dior, fashionably retro

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the letters found are read in reverse
the letters are taken in by the words that follow, so they sit inside them

explanation.surface: A hairdo has been taken up by a fashion house in a vintage style.
explanation.walkthrough: ORFA sits across 'Dior, fashionably'; 'retro' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy natural hairstyle.

clue.text: Severely punished, fellow noted

parts.note: to log something is to note it down

explanation.surface: A man was observed being punished harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be flogged is to be beaten as a harsh punishment.

clue.text: Remaining longer than guy during trip

indicators.note: the guy word happens within the trip, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a stay is a guy rope supporting a mast

explanation.surface: Someone overstays their welcome while away on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is a rope here, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to stay beyond someone else or beyond a limit.

clue.text: Greatly animated, one tears up tweeds oddly

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the tears word is reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: An excited person rips up some tweed jackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RIPS into SPIR; 'oddly' gives TED from the first, third and fifth letters of 'tweeds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means lively and full of energy.

clue.text: Aiming for main prize in Kent?

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, SE

explanation.surface: Someone competes for the top prize in a Kent contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old word for the sea. KENT is an English county in the south-east, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward means heading toward the ocean, which crosswords often call the main.

clue.text: Important achievement: former pupil, after vacation, gets round to it

indicators.note: the word is emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An ex-student back from holiday finally gets down to a big job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a school holiday, but it empties 'pupil' to PL.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or notable deed.

clue.text: Use bugging device Leninist cobbled together

indicators.note: to cobble together is to assemble roughly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soviet agents rig up a crude listening bug.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen in is to eavesdrop, which is what a bug lets you do.

clue.text: Really hot and tense after doctor appears?

indicators.note: the hot and tense letters follow the doctor word

parts.note: to doctor is to rig or tamper with
T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar

explanation.surface: A patient feels feverish and anxious once the doctor arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, 'appears' is a link. 'Really' means very, as in 'a right mess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Right can mean very or thoroughly, as in 'right royal'.

clue.text: Wealthy experts having nothing invested in country school

indicators.note: the nothing letter is put into the country word

parts.note: Peru is a South American country

explanation.surface: Rich specialists put no money into a rural school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' sounds financial but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means well off and thriving.

clue.text: Look about area of France

parts.note: Gard is a département in southern France

explanation.surface: Gaze around a French region.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it.

clue.text: Trusty soldiers likely to give support

explanation.surface: Dependable troops can be counted on to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give support' describes RE sitting on top of LIABLE in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reliable can be trusted.

clue.text: Intensely put out by the delay

indicators.note: put out means disrupted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is very annoyed by the hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like annoyed, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something heatedly is to do it with intense feeling.

clue.text: Pupil first to meet relative in urban area

indicators.note: the letters go inside the urban area word

parts.note: a town is an urban area

indicators.note: the first of the word meet means its opening letter alone is used

explanation.surface: A schoolchild goes first to meet a family member in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM BROWN is the schoolboy hero of the Victorian novel Tom Brown's Schooldays.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Tom Brown is a schoolboy at Rugby.

clue.text: White wine — half litre — served with sole (not quite enough)

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, leaving the word just short

explanation.surface: Half a litre of white wine is poured with a fish dish, but not enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the fish; it means only.
explanation.definitionFit: Sémillon is a white grape and its wine.

clue.text: Mother suppresses desire for former screen star

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down within, so the desire word is held inside

explanation.surface: A mother hides her crush on an old film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Mitchum was a Hollywood actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Mitchum was a famous film actor of the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Be close to a woman involved in racket

indicators.note: the woman is wrapped up in the racket, so placed inside it

parts.note: din is a racket or loud noise

explanation.surface: A woman is caught up in some shady scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a scam but means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin is to be next to.

clue.text: Scorer heading ball to back of crowd? That's exaggerated

indicators.note: the ball letter goes at the head, before the scorer

parts.note: O is round like a ball

indicators.note: the back of the crowd is its rear end, so only the word's final letter is used

explanation.surface: A goal-scorer heads the ball into the back of the crowd and gets carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' looks like a footballer but is a composer. 'to' and 'That's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdone has been taken too far, exaggerated.

clue.text: Subsequently secures degree in Ancient Greek

indicators.note: to secure is to hold inside, so the degree is held within

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Later someone gets a degree in classics.
explanation.definitionFit: A Theban came from Thebes in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Run into sex traffickers

indicators.note: the letters run into, across the two words

explanation.surface: Encountering people who traffic in sex.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an EXTRA is a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an extra is a run added without the batter hitting it.

clue.text: Drink is served round part of ship, I see

indicators.note: the drink goes round the ship part, holding it inside

parts.note: a hold is the cargo space of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor is handed beer in the hold.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads the speaker 'I' as one who sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is one who looks on, so the speaker who sees is one.

clue.text: Veal stew served on European holiday

indicators.note: a stew mixes ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stewed veal is on the menu on a European holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off work, a holiday.

clue.text: Raised money for speaker

indicators.note: the word as a speaker would say it, by sound

explanation.surface: Funds raised for the person giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals bred are reared or brought up.

clue.text: Loves assimilating the lines in Shakespearean drama

indicators.note: to assimilate is to take in, so the zeros take in the rest

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so loves are OO
L is the abbreviation for line, so lines are LL

explanation.surface: Someone loves taking in the lines of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is a Shakespeare tragedy.

clue.text: Maybe 18, the swine, faces left-wing revolutionary

indicators.note: revolving turns things round, so the left-wing word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A pig confronts a radical leftist.
explanation.walkthrough: 18-down, TOM BROWN, was a boarder at his school.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Brown lived at his school, so he is an example of a live-in pupil.

clue.text: Destroyed mouse almost, for sport

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so the letters are rearranged
the word stops short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A mouse nearly wrecked for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops E from 'mouse'; 'Destroyed' shuffles MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese wrestling, a sport.

clue.text: Finished with books after higher education, not as planned

indicators.note: the books and finished pieces come after the university word

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone finished reading after university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintended means not meant or planned.
